answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce, nonrefundable stake before it can vote on shared jobs. When an agent’s work is challenged, randomly selected peers check the result; verified fraud burns part of its stake, while honest checks earn a fee. This makes creating many identities useful only if the attacker funds each one and risks losing that capital, rather than gaining influence for free. A pulse of suspicious accounts can also trigger a beacon that raises review rates, while opal marks a stake tier, not a substitute for evidence.
